messages:
Claire: hey team, Claire here (first day). Quick map request: where do I drop laptop/setup errors, noisy CI chatter, design/UX asks, and product feedback? Also: any tips for muting bots without losing urgent pages, and where to keep onboarding links so I don\u2019t lose them in DMs?

Diego: welcome Claire! short map: laptop/setup -> #help (attach OS + 1-line error); noisy CI -> #build-failures (we mute this channel by default); design/UX -> #design; product feedback -> #product-feedback or the squad channel for scoped items.

Claire: nice. specific question: I got direct messages from 4 apps on joining. I want deploy/security pages, but not CI pings. 

Sasha: two options: 1) Channel-level: open the channel -> bell icon -> "Mentions & keywords". 2) App-level: Apps -> select the app -> App home -> Settings -> uncheck "Send direct messages". Note: changing App Home settings requires you to be allowed by workspace app permissions; contact Workspace Admin if the option is locked.

onboard-bot: Welcome Claire! To finish onboarding run:

```
$ rwi-init --onboard
$ rwi-auth grant
```

Reply "done" to mark items complete.

Claire: thanks. where should I pin onboarding docs vs save them personally?

Diego: pin team-level docs in your squad channel (click channel name -> "Pinned" -> add). For files you want personally, use Slack "Saved" (hover message -> Save). We also keep a canonical onboarding doc in the #devex channel app home (search "Onboarding Guide").

Claire: good tip. another etiquette question: what do you put in a first-week intro post? any format we follow?

PM: Short template we like: 1) Name / Role / Squad 2) TZ (e.g., PST) 3) What I'm working on this week 4) One fun fact. Post in #introductions and drop a 1-line in your squad channel linking any kickoff ticket or RFC. Example: "Claire | Infra Eng | PST | Working on infra onboarding improvements (RFC #123) | Likes sourdough"

Claire: perfect. about @channel vs @here vs user groups: what's allowed?

Sasha: rules: @channel = reserved for org or team-wide announcements (rare); @here = acceptable for time-sensitive asks during local working hours; user groups (e.g., @infra) = only after checking with the group owner. If in doubt, DM the lead or ask in the thread. We prefer add "[ASYNC]" tag on posts intended for non-urgent feedback.

Claire: got it. one more: when do we move from a thread -> ticket -> incident? example: flaky CI failing my PR vs customer-facing 5xxs.

Diego: flow: PR/CI failures -> channel thread (link PR/CI). If it blocks multiple people or a deploy -> open a ticket and tag #incidents if user-facing. P0/P1 outages -> incident & page @oncall. For vendor/external blockers, create a ticket and add short updates in the thread, not the other way around.

infra-bot: Reminder: pages (SEV/P0) will always use @oncall regardless of your mute settings if you keep @oncall in your notification keywords. Add keywords via Preferences -> Notifications -> Notification keywords.

Claire: awesome. last small thing: any recommended micro-habits to keep Slack tidy as a new hire?

Sasha: 1) Use threads for follow-ups, 2) use :thumbsup: for quick ACKs, 3) add links to PRs/issues in one-line context, 4) prefix longer posts with [Help]/[FYI]/[Decision], 5) pin onboarding links in your team channel and save the same in Saved items.

Claire: thank you! posting intros in #introductions and pinning the onboarding doc in my squad. appreciate the help :raised_hands:
